title: Using a decision model to create dynamic NPCs that add to the game's world
author: Brave-History-6502
selftext:
I am creating NPCs that 'exist' in my game's dynamic world. These NPC exist for the players to observe, interact with and also to add to the game world.   
  
My concept is that the NPCs contribute "art" and sculptures to the shared game world over time. As a player, you can come across something they've build, see a timelapse of their build process and even see the NPCs thought process behind the build.

Jev is used by the NPC to choose what artwork to undertake, how to vary it as they are building with "intuition" and respond to the environment around them. 

It is still a proof of concept but I think an interesting idea and also relatively cheap given jev is extremely fast and low cost.

Feel free to check it out, should be live fairly soon: [https://fjordfall.fly.dev/](https://fjordfall.fly.dev/)

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: I utilize Claude code heavily but start with simple 2d prototypes of the concept— ie can jev for example guide a 2d painting? And then scale it up from there. These particular designs are inspired by Andy goldsworthy for example. Basically the npc “artist” is given a general “taste” and then jev makes both high level and low level decisions in the implementation of each piece!
